items.q: An error message is best thought of as:
options: A precise clue about what failed and usually where
A scolding that means you're bad at this
A sign you should delete everything and start over

explain.right: An error tells you what went wrong and often the file and line — the most useful free information while building.
explain.wrong: It's not a judgment, noise, or a reason to restart; it's a readable pointer at the problem.

items.q: What's the most reliable way to get the AI to fix a bug?
options: Give the exact error + the relevant code/file + what you did + what you expected instead
Ask it repeatedly until it works

explain.right: The exact error plus the code and expected behavior narrows the model to your real problem, like a good plumber callout.
explain.wrong: Vague or repeated demands make it pattern-match to generic, often irrelevant fixes.

items.q: The AI keeps trying nearly identical fixes and the same error keeps coming back. Best move?
options: Keep letting it guess — the next try might work
Stop and add real evidence: roll back to a known-good commit, read the actual output or add a log, then reframe
Delete the whole project and start over
Accept the bug and move on

explain.right: A loop means the model lacks information; the cure is evidence (a log, a reproduction) or a rollback, not more guesses.
explain.wrong: More guessing, nuking the project, or giving up all skip the real fix: give it something true to work from.

items.q: Why does pasting the actual error and code beat saying 'it's broken'?
options: It flatters the model into trying harder
It narrows the model's prediction to your specific problem instead of a generic guess
It runs the code for you

explain.right: A vague report has many plausible continuations and few are right; the error plus code pins it to your actual bug.
explain.wrong: It's not about length or flattery, and pasting text doesn't execute anything — it's about precision.

items.q: Turn 'my app is broken' into a good fix request. What would you include?
rubric: The exact error text, copied not paraphrased
The relevant code/file (and ideally the steps that triggered it)
What you expected to happen instead

explain.right: Strong answers supply the exact error, the relevant code and trigger steps, and the expected-vs-actual behavior.
explain.wrong: A weak answer just adds 'please' or more adjectives without the concrete error and context.
